name: useradd
description: The low-level command for creating new user accounts (adduser is a friendlier interactive wrapper on Debian-based systems).

flags.description: Create the home directory /home/USERNAME and copy skeleton files from /etc/skel.
Set the login shell (e.g. -s /bin/bash). Without it, some systems default to /bin/sh.
Additional groups (comma-separated) besides the primary one.
Set an expiration date for the account (YYYY-MM-DD).

examples.explanation: Creates the user alice with a home directory and bash as the shell.
useradd does NOT set a password — the account stays locked until you run passwd.
Creates bob and immediately adds him to the docker and sudo groups.
The seven fields: name, password placeholder (x = in /etc/shadow), UID, GID, comment, home, shell.

about: useradd edits /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, and /etc/group according to the defaults in /etc/default/useradd and /etc/login.defs. On Debian/Ubuntu, adduser is an interactive script that wraps useradd with saner defaults (creates home, prompts for password). On RHEL/Fedora, adduser is usually just a symlink to useradd.
useCases: Create service accounts with specific UIDs.
Provision users in scripts with exact options.
Understand what adduser does under the hood.
mistakes: Forgetting -m — the user is created without a home directory.
Forgetting to set a password with passwd, leaving the account unusable.
warnings: Running useradd without -s on some distributions creates accounts with /bin/sh or nologin; check /etc/default/useradd for your defaults.
distroNotes: useradd comes from shadow-utils. adduser behavior differs: full interactive tool on Debian/Ubuntu, symlink to useradd on RHEL-family.
